title: Kinesiology taping
what: An elastic tape is stuck on the skin. It supports muscles and joints without limiting movement.
why: For muscle and joint pain, after injuries, for swelling, in sports, and alongside exercise therapy.
duration: applying it usually takes 10 to 20 minutes; the tape is usually worn for 3 to 5 days
tell_doctor: If you are allergic to plasters or adhesive
If your skin is sensitive, or there are wounds or a rash in that area
If you have varicose veins or bleeding problems

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Skin should be clean and dry. Do not put on cream that day.

prepare.title: Hair
prepare.text: Thick hair in the area may need to be shaved. Ask in advance.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Loose clothes, so the area can be uncovered.

bring: Your referral or doctor's report, if you have one
steps: The specialist examines you and checks your movement
The tape is measured and cut to shape
It is applied with the right tension, sometimes with the muscle stretched
The tape is rubbed with the palm so the adhesive sets
feel: A light pulling feeling on the skin
after: You can shower. Pat the tape dry with a towel afterward
Do not dry it with a hair dryer. The adhesive can overheat
Remove it slowly, in the direction of hair growth, holding the skin
If the edges peel, you can trim them carefully
red_flags: Strong itching, burning, or redness under the tape: take it off

faq.a: It helps reduce pain and support muscles, but is usually used with other treatment.
Yes, in the shower. Then just pat it dry with a towel.

reminders.text: Taping tomorrow. Skin should be clean, with no cream.
